title: Bidirectional A* in Kallio: Find the Fastest Way!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* split the search from start and goal across real street-map graphs, meeting in the middle for speed. The visualization shows how heuristics guide both frontiers to reconstruct an efficient route.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ **Bidirectional A*** is like sending two teams out—one from your start point and one from your destination—then having them *meet* where the routes most likely connect. 🤝

🧠 **Deep technical angle:** On a street-map graph, each intersection is a node and each road segment is an edge with costs. Bidirectional A* runs A* from both directions using an admissible heuristic (often based on geographic distance), tightening the search by expanding fewer states than classic A*.

🗺️ **Real-world map theory:** The Kallio road network becomes a weighted graph; the algorithm tracks two expanding frontiers, and when a node (or edge boundary) overlaps, it stops and stitches the best partial paths into a full route. The result is a cleaner, faster route discovery—especially noticeable on dense urban grids.

🎬 Want me to visualize *different heuristics* (Manhattan vs. haversine) or *time-dependent edge weights* next? Comment your route idea from Kallio and hit **share** to help more people learn graph search! 📲💡
fb_caption:
Ever wondered how a phone navigation app finds a route so quickly? 🚗💨 Bidirectional A* treats a city’s streets as a weighted graph, then searches from both the start and goal at once—reducing the explored area and meeting in the middle for an efficient path.

📌 In this reel, you’ll see frontier expansion, heuristic-driven node selection, and how the final route is reconstructed from two partial solutions. If you found it cool or educational, share it with a friend who loves coding or math—community learning matters! ❤️
